top10: Phase I comes FIRST — every scenario asking "what should the PM do first?" → understand the business problem .
"Do we even need AI?" — rules/RPA beat AI for deterministic, repetitive tasks.
Every valid AI use case maps to one of the 7 Patterns of AI — memorize all seven with examples.
Success = business KPIs and ROI , never accuracy alone.
The Go/No-Go decision is a Phase I output (P-P-K-F: Problem, Pattern, KPI, Feasibility).
Think Big, Start Small, Iterate Often — reject big-bang answers.
Phase I repeats in every iteration — it is not one-time.
Ethics, bias, and regulation are assessed in Phase I, not left for the end.
1 cause of AI project failure = poor business understanding ("solution looking for a problem").

examTips.heading: Memory Tricks
bullets: Phase I = WHY? (Phase II = WHAT data? Phase III = HOW to prepare?)
7 Patterns mnemonic: "HAPPY CPR Goals" → H yperpersonalization, A utonomous, P redictive, P atterns & Anomalies, Con v ersational, R ecognition, G oal-driven. (Or make your own — e.g., "HAP-CPRG" .)
Go/No-Go checklist: P-P-K-F (Problem, Pattern, KPI, Feasibility).
Mantra: "Think Big, Start Small, Iterate Often."

examTips.heading: Keywords That Signal the Right Answer
Common Exam Traps to Avoid
bullets: Any answer that says " start by collecting data " or " start by selecting an algorithm " in a new-project scenario → WRONG . Business understanding comes first.
Any answer implying AI should be used for simple rule-based tasks → WRONG (use RPA).
Any answer defining success only by accuracy → WRONG (need business KPI).
"Complete all requirements upfront, then build" (waterfall thinking) → WRONG (CPMAI is iterative).
